briefs.title: Fed Board releases minutes of its October 19 and October 28, 2026 discount rate meetings
briefs.summary: On November 24, 2026, the Federal Reserve Board released the minutes of its meetings to review and determine the discount rates offered to depository institutions through the discount window. The minutes cover the Board meetings held on October 19 and October 28, 2026. The Board states that its process for setting the discount rate is distinct from the process the Federal Open Market Committee follows in setting the target range for the federal funds rate. The press release text does not give any rate levels or decisions; those are in the attached PDF.

actors.reason: They borrow through the discount window, so the discount rate affects their cost of that funding, but the release text gives no rate decision.

actors.name: Federal Reserve Board of Governors
actors.reason: It sets the discount rate in its own meetings, and the minutes document those meetings.

actors.name: Federal Open Market Committee
actors.reason: It sets the federal funds rate target range through a separate process, which the Board says is distinct from the discount rate process.

watch.note: Check the PDF attachment to the Federal Reserve press release.

watch.note: Compare the Fed's posted discount window rates with prior published levels.

es.title: La Fed publica actas de sus reuniones de tasa de descuento del 19 y 28 de octubre de 2026
es.summary: El 24 de noviembre de 2026, la Junta de la Reserva Federal publicó las actas de sus reuniones para revisar y determinar las tasas de descuento ofrecidas a las instituciones depositarias a través de la ventanilla de descuento. Las actas cubren las reuniones de la Junta del 19 y el 28 de octubre de 2026. La Junta señala que su proceso para fijar la tasa de descuento es distinto del que sigue el Comité Federal de Mercado Abierto para establecer el rango objetivo de la tasa de los fondos federales. El texto del comunicado no incluye niveles de tasas ni decisiones; esos datos están en el PDF adjunto.

actors.reason: Se financian a través de la ventanilla de descuento, por lo que la tasa de descuento afecta el costo de ese financiamiento, pero el texto no informa ninguna decisión sobre tasas.

actors.reason: Fija la tasa de descuento en sus propias reuniones, que las actas documentan.

actors.name: Comité Federal de Mercado Abierto
actors.reason: Establece el rango objetivo de la tasa de los fondos federales mediante un proceso aparte, que la Junta describe como distinto del de la tasa de descuento.

watch.note: Consultar el archivo PDF adjunto al comunicado de la Reserva Federal.

briefs.title: BanRep's Villar says 2027 minimum wage rise should reflect inflation plus productivity
briefs.summary: Banco de la República manager Leonardo Villar said at the launch of the OECD Economic Survey: Colombia 2026 that the minimum wage increase should return to adjustments in line with the economic situation. He said inflation could end this year at around 6% or 7% and that an effort is needed to bring inflation lower next year. Villar cited a Constitutional Court ruling that the increase must be at least equal to observed inflation, with a component for productivity added. He also said a technical decision would help the central bank avoid keeping such a restrictive policy.

actors.name: Banco de la República
actors.reason: Villar said a technical wage decision would mean the bank does not have to keep such a restrictive policy, so the outcome could affect its policy stance.

actors.name: Minimum wage workers
actors.reason: Villar said real wages rise more if inflation falls than if the decision adds upward inflation pressure.

actors.name: Employers
actors.reason: They take part in the wage negotiation table, and the size of the increase will determine their labor costs.

watch.note: Compare the announced percentage with year-end inflation reported by the statistics office.

es.title: Villar (BanRep): alza del salario mínimo 2027 debería reflejar inflación y productividad
es.summary: El gerente del Banco de la República, Leonardo Villar, dijo en el lanzamiento del Economic Survey: Colombia 2026 de la OCDE que se debe volver a ajustes acordes con la situación económica. Señaló que la inflación podría terminar este año alrededor del 6 % o 7 % y que se requiere un esfuerzo para que el próximo año sea más baja. Villar citó una sentencia de la Corte Constitucional según la cual el aumento debe ser, cuando menos, igual a la inflación observada, a lo que debe sumarse un componente de productividad. También afirmó que una decisión técnica ayudaría a que el Banco no tenga que mantener una política tan restrictiva.

briefs.title: EIA explains how it converts different energy sources to Btu to compare them
briefs.summary: EIA says it converts production and consumption of different resources to British thermal units (Btu) so they can be compared. For combustible fuels it uses thermal conversion factors that it updates each year, and it publishes heat content data for more than 30 petroleum products, 4 types of coal, and natural gas. For hydro, wind, solar and geothermal it applies a constant heat content of electricity of 3,412 Btu/kWh. Since 2001, heat rates for coal and petroleum generation have risen slightly, while the rate for natural gas has gone down.

actors.reason: Knowing the conversion methods helps them interpret EIA comparisons across fuels, but the source does not describe any specific effect.

actors.reason: The source says the heat rate for gas generation has fallen since 2001, partly due to more efficient combined-cycle plants, meaning less energy used per kWh.

es.title: La EIA explica cómo convierte distintas fuentes de energía a Btu para poder compararlas
es.summary: La EIA indica que convierte la producción y el consumo de distintos recursos a unidades térmicas británicas (Btu) para poder compararlos. Para los combustibles que se queman usa factores de conversión térmica que actualiza cada año, y publica datos de poder calórico de más de 30 productos derivados del petróleo, 4 tipos de carbón y el gas natural. Para la hidroenergía, la eólica, la solar y la geotérmica aplica un contenido calórico constante de la electricidad de 3.412 Btu/kWh. Desde 2001, las tasas de consumo térmico de la generación con carbón y petróleo han subido levemente, mientras que la del gas natural ha bajado.

briefs.title: CARF says rescue law alone would not stabilize debt, sees net debt at 78.1% of GDP in 2030
briefs.summary: Colombia's Autonomous Committee on the Fiscal Rule (CARF) presented its analysis of the government's economic rescue law. It says the measures would help correct the fiscal imbalance and moderate the pace of borrowing, but net debt would keep rising to 78.1% of GDP in 2030. The Finance Ministry expects debt to stabilize at 64% of GDP, counting positive macroeconomic effects and measures outside the law. CARF estimates the law contributes 1.9% of GDP in 2027 and an average of 3.15% between 2028 and 2030, assuming no indirect macroeconomic effect and excluding unregulated measures.

actors.reason: CARF backs the size of the proposed adjustment as a minimum but questions whether the law alone, as the government's projection assumes, can stabilize debt.

actors.reason: CARF asks that any change reducing the law's fiscal effect during the legislative process be offset by equivalent measures.

es.title: CARF: la ley de rescate no basta para estabilizar la deuda, que llegaría a 78,1 % del PIB en 2030
es.summary: El Comité Autónomo de la Regla Fiscal (CARF) presentó su análisis de la ley de rescate económico del Gobierno. Señala que las medidas ayudarían a corregir el desbalance fiscal y a moderar el ritmo de endeudamiento, pero que la deuda neta seguiría aumentando hasta 78,1 % del PIB en 2030. El Ministerio de Hacienda prevé estabilizar la deuda en 64 % del PIB, al incluir impactos macroeconómicos positivos y medidas externas a la ley. El CARF calcula que la ley aporta 1,9 % del PIB en 2027 y un promedio de 3,15 % entre 2028 y 2030, con efecto macroeconómico indirecto nulo y sin contar medidas no reglamentadas.

briefs.title: US consumer confidence rises to 103.3 in November; inflation worries persist
briefs.summary: The Conference Board's consumer confidence index rose to 103.3 in November, up 11.4 points from October and well above the Dow Jones consensus of 92.2. The board said confidence among Democrats and independents improved sharply, while confidence among Republicans fell slightly. Twelve-month inflation expectations fell for a second straight month but remained high at 5.7%. The share of respondents seeing jobs as 'plentiful' rose to 30.8% from 26.2%, while 'hard to get' fell to 18.4%.

es.title: Confianza del consumidor en EE. UU. sube a 103,3 en noviembre; persiste la preocupación por inflación
es.summary: El índice de confianza del consumidor del Conference Board subió a 103,3 en noviembre, 11,4 puntos más que en octubre y muy por encima del consenso de Dow Jones de 92,2. La entidad indicó que la confianza de demócratas e independientes mejoró con fuerza, mientras que la de los republicanos cayó levemente. Las expectativas de inflación a 12 meses bajaron por segundo mes consecutivo, pero siguen altas, en 5,7%. La proporción de encuestados que consideran los empleos «abundantes» subió a 30,8% desde 26,2%, y la de «difíciles de conseguir» bajó a 18,4%.

briefs.title: Nvidia shares up 31.97% on Colombia's Global Market as Colcap rises 2.02% on Nov 23
briefs.summary: Valora Analitik reports that the MSCI Colcap closed on November 23, 2026 at 2,345.96 points, up 2.02%, with a year-to-date gain of 13.44%. Equity trading volume was COP 224,284 million, down 15.40% from COP 265,106 million the previous session. In the Mercado Global Colombiano, NVIDIA Corporation (NVDACO) rose 31.97% on volume of COP 18,281 million, the most traded asset in that market. audit.title: Fed Board releases minutes of its October 19 and October 28, 2026 discount rate meetings

issues: Minor: the summary states that rate levels and decisions 'are in the attached PDF' (ES: 'esos datos están en el PDF adjunto'). The source only lists an 'Attachment (PDF)' and does not describe its contents. Suggest rewording to 'the minutes themselves are provided as an attached PDF' in both language versions.

audit.title: BanRep's Villar says 2027 minimum wage rise should reflect inflation plus productivity

issues: Actor 'Employers' / 'Empresarios': the reason says the size of the increase 'will determine their labor costs' ('determinará sus costos laborales'). The source does not say this. It only says employers take part in the negotiation table, so this impact claim is unsupported.

Minor: the Spanish summary's first sentence says 'se debe volver a ajustes acordes con la situación económica' without naming the minimum wage increase, while the English names it explicitly. It is not a contradiction, but adding 'del salario mínimo' would align the two versions.

audit.title: EIA explains how it converts different energy sources to Btu to compare them

issues: The 'favorable' impact for natural gas-fired generators is not supported by the source. EIA only reports that the aggregate heat rate for gas generation has declined since 2001, partly due to more efficient combined-cycle plants. It says nothing about any benefit to generators, such as costs, margins or competitiveness. The impact should be 'undetermined', or the actor should be removed.

The 'adverse' impact for coal and petroleum-fired generators is not supported by the source. EIA only says their heat rates have 'risen slightly' since 2001. It gives no cause and states no effect on these generators. The impact should be 'undetermined', or the actor should be removed.

Minor: the summary's '3,412 Btu/kWh' for hydro, wind, solar and geothermal is supported, but the source frames this as the 'captured energy approach'. Naming the method would be more precise. This is not a factual error.

audit.title: CARF says rescue law alone would not stabilize debt, sees net debt at 78.1% of GDP in 2030

issues: The Government (Finance Ministry) actor reason says CARF questions whether 'the law alone, as the government's projection assumes, can stabilize debt' (ES: 'como supone la proyección del Gobierno'). The source contradicts this. The government's 64% of GDP projection explicitly includes positive macroeconomic effects and measures outside the law (decrees, National Development Plan), so it does not assume the law alone stabilizes debt. Rephrase in both versions, for example: 'CARF backs the size of the proposed adjustment as a minimum but says the law alone would not stabilize debt, unlike the government's projection, which relies on macroeconomic effects and measures outside the law.'
